acceptance: Cleanup keeps its own reference to the throughput result/outstanding futures, independent of phase building
An end-to-end adapter.run_benchmark test with a deliberately hung stream asserts close_connection is not called until the stream finishes
Normal (no-timeout) runs still close the connection synchronously
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review (develop 8ed0c64e1). Consensus finding from two reviewers; call order verified directly.
description:
`_build_execution_phases` (benchbox/platforms/base/result_capture.py:1967-1969) clears `self._last_throughput_test_result` after building the phase. It runs at adapter.py:1103, before the `finally` block calls `_close_run_connection()` (adapter.py:1235, 1279-1288). That method passes the now-None attribute to `_defer_connection_close_until_quiescent`, which closes immediately when given None (adapter.py:1238-1240).

Effect: on the normal path, whenever a throughput stream times out, the shared connection (DuckDB, SQLite, Spark) is closed under a still-running stream's cursor. This breaks the concurrency ADR rule that owned resources are not reused or closed while outstanding. The deferred-close thread added for containment never runs in a full benchmark run. Existing tests patch `_close_run_connection` out, so none covers this.

Verified by reading the call order and reproduced by two reviewers (outstanding future + `_post_measurement_contained=True` -> close_connection called synchronously).
